video.title: Task Priority, currentPriority & Priority Inheritance | Day 275
video.description:
Learn to explain how to talk about how urgent a task is, how to read it and how child tasks get it: Task Priority, currentPriority & Priority Inheritance, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Task Priority - A hint that tells the system how urgent a task is, such as high, medium or low.
currentPriority - A static property that tells you the priority of the task running right now.
Priority Inheritance - The rule that a new child task starts with the same priority as the task that created it.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

Explain Task Priority, currentPriority & Priority Inheritance in iOS by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.

Task Priority - A hint that tells the system how urgent a task is, such as high, medium or low.
한국어: Task Priority: 태스크가 얼마나 급한지(high, medium, low 등) 시스템에 알려 주는 힌트

Priority Inheritance - The rule that a new child task starts with the same priority as the task that created it.
한국어: Priority Inheritance: 새 자식 태스크가 자신을 만든 태스크와 같은 우선순위로 시작하는 규칙

landscape.hook: Can you explain Task Priority, currentPriority and Priority Inheritance in English?

dialogue.title: Which task should run first?
dialogue.setting: A slow screen during a big import

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, the screen feels slow while the big import runs.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Did you set a task priority? The import should not be urgent.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No. I used the default for everything.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Give the import a low task priority. It is a hint that tells the system how urgent a task is.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And how can I check what a task got?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I did. The child task shows `high` too, but I never set that.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That is priority inheritance. A child starts with the priority of its parent.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So one high parent makes every child urgent?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, unless you create a detached task, which does not inherit it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Got it. Priority inheritance explains it, so I will lower the parent task priority.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then print currentPriority again to verify.
Give the image import a low task priority.
